lines.text: Mind your feet that side. Hot scale down there and it goes through a boot sole.
If it's the warm floor you've come about, ask away, only ask me while I'm working. The bellows are on your left. Pull when I nod and not before.
Put your hand flat on the floor. Go on. By the anvil, where the flagstone's worn smooth.

Warm, isn't it. My forge is cold till I light it after noon, so that's not where it's coming from. A vent comes up hot for an hour and then it's done with you, and this floor has never come up like that.
The men underground call it the warm shell below. Go up and look at the shrine at the shaft head.
You got up to the shrine, then. Take a candle next time and look along an edge where a plate's chipped. Those plates aren't cut stone. They're shell.
I had a broken piece on this bench a month and put it back in the scrap. Ask Gerta for her log.
Right. So you got down to the deep shrine.
Kilnback. The word cut on it, in the old letters. Somebody went into that reach and cut a name into a plate wider across than my doors, a long while before my father's father.
I've had my hand flat on that flagstone in every season there is and it comes up the same every time.
Go down when the vents are quiet. Take something at home in water or made out of rock, because nothing else will take a fire. Mind the last ladder, third rung's split.

So one of yours has aged out. You'll have the relic on you and it'll be warm still. What it's for is this: I set it into a collar-piece, plain brass, and the seat gets cut to the relic and not the other way about.
Bring it here and come back through the town tomorrow.
The young one that wears it carries some of what the old one had. How much, I couldn't tell you. Wants a day and a night in the ash before I'll have it off the bench.
There you are. Collar's cooled through and the seat's tight.
Get your thumb on the relic and try to shift it. You won't. I've put the old one's name underneath, against the strap, the same as on all of them.
Fifth shaft's open as of this spring.

There's enough coming off the steppe to keep a crew fed while they dig, and Cragmar are grazing the high scarp again. My brother's lad has gone on the new shaft and I've had him on the hammer since the start of the week.
Fourth shaft's boarded up now. It didn't fall in. There's been next to nothing off the steppe these two seasons and somebody in an office signed a paper.
I said my piece up at the office and they left the third open. Six days in seven I'm down it.
One reading a shift, off the wall of the third shaft. Thirty-one years of it now. It was nobody's job.
The shift before mine kept saying the third was warmer than the fourth and I wanted to know if they had it right. Off the wall, not out of the air, because the air moves and the wall doesn't.
Bram's sent you up for the log. Here. One reading a shift, all of them mine, off the wall and not out of the air, and the same spot on the wall every time.
Eight over the fourth. Same depth, the two shafts, so the two compare.
The eight has moved twice. It went to fourteen in two winters out of thirty-one years, four days at a stretch each time, and both followed a summer with no vent flare.
Go down the warm reach before you take the log back. There's a shrine at the bottom, not like the ones at the shaft head. Put your hand flat on it and tell me what you get.
There's a survey wants doing up on the steppe and I'm below all week.

Five I want numbers on, all up on Cinder Steppe. Ashvole, Cragmar, Pyrelisk, Stonewing, Carricrow. Hurry and you'll put the same Carricrow down in two places, because they won't settle anywhere for long. It's a full day.
And walk the west scarp. How far up the green gets now, against the old cairn.
Start at the west scarp, then the vent line, then the low ground coming back. Same order I walked it, so your figures sit by my old ones. If the vent line's flaring, leave it and come another day.
All right. It was a whole day I was asking for, and that's a lot to ask of somebody who's just walked in. Find me at the third shaft head if you get a day spare.
Carricrow first. They only settle where something's died lately, so a high Carricrow figure sends me to the other four.

Snell has it that the warmth off that scarp comes up out of the vents. I've read that wall one reading a shift since before the fourth shaft opened, same spot every time, and it has not moved. Whatever took the Stonewing off, it wasn't the ground.

Your five go in the log tonight, at the back, beside my old ones. The green against the old cairn goes in the front, with how far up it gets and what the Ashvole and Cragmar graze off it. If the green goes off that scarp I'd sooner have it off the cairn than off the birds.
